q-52230.name: Question 1
q-52230.problem: Given that ${p}^{2}-4p+4=0,$ what are the values of $p?$
q-52230.worked_solution:
First, notice that the left-hand side is a perfect square. It just needs to be factored:

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{2}-4p+4 & =0 \\ {p}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot p+{2}^{2} & =0 \\ (p-2)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(p-2)^{2}} & =\sqrt{0} \\ |p-2| & =0 \\ p-2 & =0 \\ p & =2\end{aligned}
$$

q-79160.name: Question 2
q-79160.problem: Consider the equation $(x-5)^{2}-8=2n.$ For which values of $n$ does this equation have no real solutions?
q-79160.worked_solution:
Let's try and solve using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-5)^{2}-8 & =2n \\ (x-5)^{2} & =2n+8 \\ \sqrt{(x-5)^{2}} & =\sqrt{2n+8} \\ |x-5| & =\sqrt{2n+8}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation will have no real solutions if the expression under the square root is negative, which gives the following condition:

$$
2n+8<0
$$

We solve this inequality for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2n+8 & <0 \\ 2n & <-8 \\ n & <\frac{-8}{2} \\ n & <-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, any value of $n$ that is less than $-4$ will give an equation with no real solutions.

q-218515.name: Question 3
q-218515.worked_solution:
Let's try and solve using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{3} & =h \\ {y}^{2} & =h-\frac{1}{3} \\ \sqrt{{y}^{2}} & =\sqrt{h-\frac{1}{3}} \\ |y| & =\sqrt{h-\frac{1}{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation will have no real solutions if the expression under the square root is negative, which gives the following condition:

$$
h-\frac{1}{3}<0
$$

We solve this inequality for $h:$

$$
\begin{aligned}h-\frac{1}{3} & <0 \\ h & <\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, any value of $h$ that is less than $\frac{1}{3}$ will give an equation with no real solutions.
